subject: math
intro: I'm Ms. Chen. Let's plan an 8th grade lesson on rigid transformations.

beats.narration: Informal names first, then the formal vocabulary.
This standard is about verifying the properties of rotations, reflections, and translations.
"Verify" is the key verb in the standard, so it's the key verb here too.
beats.text: Students will be able to perform translations, reflections, and rotations on the coordinate plane and verify that lengths and angles are preserved.

beats.narration: Patterns in art get students thinking about transformations before any vocabulary.
beats.text: Show a quilt pattern and ask: "How could you describe moving one tile to create the whole pattern?"

beats.narration: Patty paper makes the motion physical; measuring each time builds the idea of "rigid."
beats.text: Model each transformation with patty paper on a coordinate grid. After each one, measure a side and an angle before and after to show they match.

beats.narration: Swapping makes the rules a communication tool, not just a procedure.
beats.text: Pairs create a design by transforming a shape three times, record the coordinate rules, and swap with another pair who must identify each transformation.

beats.narration: The "what stayed the same" question checks the verification part.
beats.text: Reflect triangle A(1,2), B(4,2), C(1,5) over the y-axis. List the new coordinates. What stayed the same?

outro: Art, hands-on modeling, design, check. Your turn to plan.
